sentences.text: MAN: Good morning
sentences.zh: MAN: 早上好

sentences.text: WOMAN: Hi, this is Michelin Meyer.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 你好，我是米歇尔·迈耶。

sentences.text: I'm renting your house on Archwood Avenue.
sentences.zh: 我租了你们位于阿奇伍德大道的房子。

sentences.text: I'm due to move in next week.
sentences.zh: 我预计下周搬进去。

sentences.text: MAN: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: MAN: 哦，是的。

sentences.text: Hello, Ms.
sentences.zh: 你好，女士。

sentences.text: Meyer.
sentences.zh: 迈耶。

sentences.text: What can I do for you?
sentences.zh: 有什么可以帮您的吗？

sentences.text: WOMAN: When I viewed the house, I told you I'll most probably need to rent some furniture, at least until I know whether my temporary work contract is going to be made permanent.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 我看房时曾告诉过您，我极有可能需要租一些家具，至少在确定我的临时工作合同是否会转为长期合同之前都需要。

sentences.text: MAN: Yes, of course.
sentences.zh: MAN: 是的，当然可以。

sentences.text: I remember.
sentences.zh: 我记得。

sentences.text: And I said I could give you some information about furniture rental companies in the city.
sentences.zh: 我当时说可以给您提供一些本市家具租赁公司的信息。

sentences.text: WOMAN: That's right.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 没错。

sentences.text: MAN: Well, the biggest company is called Peak Rentals.
sentences.zh: MAN: 嗯，最大的一家公司叫峰顶租赁公司（Peak Rentals）。

sentences.text: I've recommended them to other people and have always heard positive reports about them.
sentences.zh: 我曾向其他人推荐过他们，而且一直听到关于他们的正面评价。

sentences.text: WOMAN: Could you give me an idea of their costs?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 您能大概告诉我他们的收费情况吗？

sentences.text: MAN: Sure.
sentences.zh: MAN: 当然可以。

sentences.text: I actually have one of their brochures here.
sentences.zh: 我这儿正好有一份他们的宣传册。

sentences.text: It says the monthly price per room starts at $105 and goes up to $239.
sentences.zh: 上面写着每间房的月租金从105美元起，最高达239美元。

sentences.text: That depends on which rooms you need furniture for, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，具体价格取决于您需要为哪些房间配备家具。

sentences.text: WOMAN: Sure.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 当然。

sentences.text: It's just to get a general idea of how much it's going to cost.
sentences.zh: 这只是为了大致了解一下费用会是多少。

sentences.text: And you said you had some positive feedback about this company?
sentences.zh: 而且您说您对这家公司有一些正面反馈？

sentences.text: MAN: Yes.
sentences.zh: MAN: 是的。

sentences.text: People have mentioned that the furniture from Peak Rentals is more modern than any of the other companies.
sentences.zh: 人们提到Peak Rentals公司的家具比其他任何公司的都要更现代。

sentences.text: And also, once you place an order, the furniture will be delivered to you in just one or two days.
sentences.zh: 此外，一旦您下了订单，家具将在一到两天内送货上门。

sentences.text: WOMAN: That would be really helpful.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 这确实会非常有帮助。

sentences.text: MAN: Oh, and the brochure says that there's a special offer at the moment.
sentences.zh: MAN: 哦，还有，宣传册上说目前有一项特别优惠。

sentences.text: If you rent living room furniture, I believe that's a set of chairs and a TV table, you'll also get a lamp at no extra cost.
sentences.zh: 如果您租用客厅家具——我相信这包括一套椅子和一张电视桌——您还将免费获赠一盏台灯。

sentences.text: WOMAN: Okay, but you know, that price range you gave is more than I was hoping to pay.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 好的，但您知道，您刚才给出的这个价格区间比我原本希望支付的要高。

sentences.text: MAN: Then you could try Aaron and Oliver.
sentences.zh: MAN: 那您可以试试Aaron和Oliver公司。

sentences.text: WOMAN: Sorry, what and Oliver?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 抱歉，是‘什么’和Oliver？

sentences.text: MAN: Aaron, double A-R-O-N
sentences.zh: MAN: Aaron，双A-R-O-N。

sentences.text: WOMAN: OK, are they cheaper
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 好的，他们更便宜吗？

sentences.text: MAN: I say they are a mid company But if you chose them you need to be aware that they charge an extra 12 every month in case of damage
sentences.zh: MAN: 我觉得他们属于中等价位的公司。但如果您选择他们，需要注意的是，他们每月会额外收取12英镑，以应对可能发生的损坏。

sentences.text: WOMAN: Oh, I see.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 哦，我明白了。

sentences.text: I'd have to do the math carefully then.
sentences.zh: 那我就得仔细算一算了。

sentences.text: MAN: Right.
sentences.zh: MAN: 没错。

sentences.text: But one helpful thing is that they also do cleaning for customers.
sentences.zh: 但有一点很有帮助：他们也为客户提供清洁服务。

sentences.text: WOMAN: For the furniture?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 是为家具清洁吗？

sentences.text: MAN: For the house.
sentences.zh: MAN: 为了房子。

sentences.text: WOMAN: Oh, I see.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 哦，我明白了。

sentences.text: I probably won't need that.
sentences.zh: 我可能不需要那个。

sentences.text: MAN: There's another company called Larch Furniture.
sentences.zh: MAN: 还有一家公司叫山毛榉家具公司。

sentences.text: It's quite new, and it has the lowest prices in town.
sentences.zh: 这家公司很新，而且是镇上价格最低的。

sentences.text: That's for both furniture and also electronic equipment.
sentences.zh: 这既包括家具，也包括电子设备。

sentences.text: WOMAN: Well, that would be good.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 嗯，那倒不错。

sentences.text: I'm not bringing much with me, and I won't have much time to go shopping after I start my job.
sentences.zh: 我不会带太多东西过去，而且开始工作后，我也没多少时间去购物。

sentences.text: MAN: There are two things you need to know about large furniture.
sentences.zh: MAN: 关于大型家具，您需要了解两点。

sentences.text: First of all you have to take out insurance on the furniture and you need to organize that yourself
sentences.zh: 首先，您必须为家具购买保险，而且需要您自己办理。

sentences.text: WOMAN: That wouldn't be too hard.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 那应该不会太难。

sentences.text: MAN: Also you can take out a contract for less than six months but I figure that might not be a problem for you.
sentences.zh: MAN: 此外，您也可以签订不足六个月的租赁合同，不过我想这对您来说可能不是问题。

sentences.text: You're renting the house for 12 months after all, aren't you?
sentences.zh: 毕竟您租这套房子为期12个月，对吧？

sentences.text: WOMAN: Yes, okay.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 是的，好的。

sentences.text: Well, I...
sentences.zh: 嗯，我……

sentences.text: MAN: Sorry to interrupt.
sentences.zh: MAN: 抱歉打断一下。

sentences.text: I just thought of another furniture rental company.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚又想到另一家家具租赁公司。

sentences.text: It's called Space Rentals, and it's located very near to the house.
sentences.zh: 它叫空间租赁公司，位置离您要租的房子非常近。

sentences.text: WOMAN: Okay.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 好的。

sentences.text: MAN: I don't have any information about their charges, so it's best to use their app to find out what it would cost you to use them.
sentences.zh: MAN: 我没有关于他们收费标准的任何信息，所以最好使用他们的应用程序来查询您使用其服务所需支付的费用。

sentences.text: WOMAN: Okay, thanks.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 好的，谢谢。

sentences.text: I'll do that.
sentences.zh: 我会照做的。

sentences.text: MAN: One good thing about that company is that if you don't like the furniture once it's delivered, you can request exchanges, as long as you do that within a week of receiving it.
sentences.zh: MAN: 那家公司一个很大的优点是：一旦家具送达后您不满意，只要在收货后一周内提出，就可以申请更换。

sentences.text: WOMAN: That sounds really great.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 听起来真不错。

sentences.text: Okay, well, thanks very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，非常感谢。

sentences.text: That's so helpful
sentences.zh: 这真是太有帮助了。

sentences.text: Hello, I'm Hayden.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是海登。

sentences.text: I'm one of the archaeologists investigating the site here at Bidcuster.
sentences.zh: 我是正在比德卡斯特遗址开展考古调查的考古学家之一。

sentences.text: This is the third summer for this community project, and most of the people digging here are volunteers.
sentences.zh: 这是这个社区项目的第三个夏季，现场大部分挖掘人员都是志愿者。

sentences.text: I'm a full -time archaeologist for the town council, but I was asked to join the project by NHA, a charity which sets up projects like this up and down the country.
sentences.zh: 我是镇议会的全职考古学家，但应全国性慈善机构NHA的邀请加入了该项目，该机构在全国各地设立此类项目。

sentences.text: As you can see, we're next to Bidcaster Castle, which is great because the owners let us use their facilities.
sentences.zh: 如您所见，我们紧邻比德卡斯特城堡，这非常有利，因为城堡主人允许我们使用他们的设施。

sentences.text: So, how did we get to where we are today?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们是如何走到今天这一步的呢？

sentences.text: MAN: y archaeology projects happen when an ancient object is found, and in our case that object was a gold coin.
sentences.zh: MAN：大多数考古项目始于发现古代器物，而我们的项目正是由一枚金币的发现引发的。

sentences.text: Coins are often found by people using metal detectors to look for things buried in the ground or coins are uncovered when wild animals like rabbits have been digging tunnels.
sentences.zh: 硬币常由使用金属探测器搜寻地下埋藏物品的人发现，或由兔子等野生动物挖洞时偶然暴露出来。

sentences.text: Here, a walker found it on the ground after a rainstorm washed away some of the earth and sand.
sentences.zh: 在这里，一名徒步者在一场暴雨冲走部分泥土和沙子后，在地面上发现了这枚金币。

sentences.text: When the story of the gold coin hit the news, Peter Swift, an amateur historian, contacted me to say he believed there had been a village on this site, centuries before the castle was built.
sentences.zh: 当这枚金币的消息登上新闻后，业余历史学家彼得·斯威夫特联系了我，表示他相信在城堡建成数世纪之前，此地曾存在一座村庄。

sentences.text: Just by chance, the team found some old maps and documents in our library, which showed 500 -year-old drawings of ruined buildings on the grassy area between the outer stone walls of the castle and the river.
sentences.zh: 巧合的是，团队在我们的图书馆中找到了一些古老地图和文献，其中显示城堡外围石墙与河流之间的草地曾有500年前的废墟建筑绘图。

sentences.text: We knew then we were onto something.
sentences.zh: 那时我们就意识到，我们可能有了重大发现。

sentences.text: Over the three summers the team has been here, we've found the remains of several buildings, and more broken pots than you can count.
sentences.zh: 过去三个夏季，团队在此发掘出多座建筑遗迹，以及数不胜数的破碎陶器。

sentences.text: Normally you'd expect to find brooches and other jewellery, but we're still waiting to uncover any such items.
sentences.zh: 通常人们会期待发现胸针及其他珠宝首饰，但我们至今尚未发掘出任何此类物品。

sentences.text: The people who once lived here were skilled at making tools from animal bones, as you'll see when you visit the exhibition.
sentences.zh: 曾居住于此的人们擅长用动物骨骼制作工具，您参观展览时将亲眼见到这些工具。

sentences.text: Besides the discovery of the village, we've also found evidence of human activity on the other side of the river.
sentences.zh: 除发现这座村庄外，我们在河对岸还发现了人类活动的证据。

sentences.text: No other houses or huts so far, but we can see the borders of an ancient field system.
sentences.zh: 目前尚未发现其他房屋或小屋，但我们已能辨识出一处古代农田系统的边界。

sentences.text: At one point we found a long wall and thought it was an ancient palace, but it turned out to be a modern wall.
sentences.zh: 曾有一次，我们发现了一堵长墙，一度以为是古代宫殿，结果证实是一堵现代墙体。

sentences.text: This summer's work will end soon, but we'll be back next summer.
sentences.zh: 今年夏季的工作即将结束，但我们明年夏天还会回来。

sentences.text: In the meantime, we're putting on a series of guided tours for school groups this autumn.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，今年秋季我们将为学校团体举办一系列导览参观活动。

sentences.text: Oh, and maybe you saw the TV documentary about our project.
sentences.zh: 哦，也许你们看过关于我们项目的电视纪录片。

sentences.text: That suggests the objects we've found are going to the town's museum, but we don't know that for sure yet.
sentences.zh: 这表明我们发现的文物将送往镇上的博物馆，但目前我们还不能确定。

sentences.text: When you enter the site, please make sure you keep to the paths at all times.
sentences.zh: 进入遗址时，请务必始终沿指定路径行走。

sentences.text: There are a few other things, the highlights of the site if you like, that I want to mention.
sentences.zh: 还有几处其他地点，可以说是遗址的亮点，我想提一下。

sentences.text: Take a look at the map.
sentences.zh: 请看一下地图。

sentences.text: Our present location is marked at the bottom.
sentences.zh: 我们当前的位置标在地图底部。

sentences.text: This year, we've identified the foundations of an ancient bridge, and it's really exciting today because a team of divers are in the river searching for lost objects.
sentences.zh: 今年，我们已确认了一座古桥的地基，今天尤其令人兴奋，因为一支潜水队正在河中搜寻失落的文物。

sentences.text: To reach the bridge, take the main path ahead of you, go straight on, and keep going till the path bends to the left.
sentences.zh: 要到达这座桥，请沿您前方的主路前行，一直向前走，直到道路向左转弯。

sentences.text: You'll see a smaller track leading off to the right.
sentences.zh: 您会看到一条较小的小径向右分岔。

sentences.text: Follow that to take you to the river, where the divers are.
sentences.zh: 沿这条小径前行，即可抵达潜水员所在的河边。

sentences.text: You might be interested to see the rubbish pit.
sentences.zh: 您可能对垃圾坑感兴趣。

sentences.text: This is very near the castle walls in the north -west corner of the site.
sentences.zh: 它位于遗址西北角、靠近城堡城墙的位置。

sentences.text: It actually dates to the time of the castle and not the ancient village.
sentences.zh: 它的年代实际上可追溯至城堡时期，而非古代村落时期。

sentences.text: We found oyster shells and fish bones, and we assumed they were thrown from the castle kitchen above.
sentences.zh: 我们发现了牡蛎壳和鱼骨，推测它们是从上方城堡厨房丢弃下来的。

sentences.text: One area we excavated in the first summer uncovered the site of a meeting hall.
sentences.zh: 第一个夏季发掘的一个区域，发现了会议厅的遗址。

sentences.text: We knew it was an important building because it had two rows of post holes, deep enough to support a large roof.
sentences.zh: 我们认定这是一座重要建筑，因为它有两排柱洞，深度足以支撑一个大型屋顶。

sentences.text: It is the largest structure in the central area of the site next to the current excavation area.
sentences.zh: 它是遗址中心区域最大的建筑，紧邻当前的发掘区。

sentences.text: Last year we discovered a fish pond in the ancient village.
sentences.zh: 去年我们在古代村落中发现了一个鱼塘。

sentences.text: Normally these were beside a river.
sentences.zh: 通常这类鱼塘都建在河边。

sentences.text: The pond here is further away, but it's possible the river has moved slightly.
sentences.zh: 此处的鱼塘离河较远，但有可能是河流略微改道所致。

sentences.text: Anyway, to get there from here, you turn right at the first information board you come to and follow the path into the trees.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，从这里出发，你走到第一个信息牌时向右转，然后沿着小路进入树林。

sentences.text: Before you come out of the trees, you'll see it on your right.
sentences.zh: 在你走出树林之前，它会在你的右侧。

sentences.text: If you reach the river, you've gone too far.
sentences.zh: 如果你到达了河边，那就走得太远了。

sentences.text: So, does anyone have...
sentences.zh: 那么，有人有……

sentences.text: MAYA: So, Finn, I've done as much as I can for our project on theatre programmes.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 好了，芬恩，关于我们关于戏剧节目单的项目，我已经尽我所能完成了。

sentences.text: How's your research coming along?
sentences.zh: 你的研究进展如何？

sentences.text: FINN: OK, Maya.
sentences.zh: FINN: 好的，玛雅。

sentences.text: I didn't know theatre programmes are called playbills in the USA till I started looking into the topic.
sentences.zh: 直到我开始深入研究这个主题，我才得知戏剧节目单在美国被称为‘演出广告单’（playbills）。

sentences.text: Even though I struggled to find man: y useful websites, I'm glad we picked this subject.
sentences.zh: 尽管我费了不少劲才找到许多有用的网站，但我很高兴我们选了这个课题。

sentences.text: No one else on the course is doing the same as us, although it is one of the research areas of the module convener.
sentences.zh: 课程上没有其他人做和我们相同的课题，尽管这恰好是本模块负责教师的研究领域之一。

sentences.text: MAYA: That might actually put some people off.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 这反倒可能让一些人望而却步。

sentences.text: FINN: I suppose so.
sentences.zh: FINN: 我想确实如此。

sentences.text: Anyway I hadn't realised there are actually companies specialising in creating theatre programmes
sentences.zh: 不过，我之前根本没意识到，居然真有公司专门从事戏剧节目单的设计与制作。

sentences.text: MAYA: Yes they are quite common nowadays.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 是的，如今这类公司已相当普遍。

sentences.text: Contrary to what man: y people think, theatres don't hire people to do the programmes.
sentences.zh: 与许多人所想的相反，剧院并不会雇人来制作节目单。

sentences.text: In fact, companies buy the rights to publish programmes on the theatre's behalf and then make their money selling advertising space within the programme booklet.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这些公司会向剧院购买授权，代表剧院出版节目单，然后通过在节目册内出售广告位来盈利。

sentences.text: FINN: It must be easier for theatres to do it that way.
sentences.zh: FINN: 对剧院来说，这样操作肯定更简便。

sentences.text: MAYA: Yes.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 没错。

sentences.text: FINN: I remember reading something about programmes in early British theatre.
sentences.zh: FINN: 我记得曾读到过有关英国早期戏剧节目单的内容。

sentences.text: It said that the cast was always very important.
sentences.zh: 文中提到，演员阵容始终至关重要。

sentences.text: MAYA: Yeah, audiences were very familiar with leading actors and big names would draw huge crowds.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 是啊，观众对当红主演和知名演员都非常熟悉，大牌明星往往能吸引大量观众。

sentences.text: FINN: But I hadn't realised that if the programme named a famous actor, that's who the public expected to perform.
sentences.zh: FINN: 但我之前并不知道，只要节目单上列出了某位著名演员的名字，公众就理所当然地认为此人一定会登台演出。

sentences.text: And if that didn't happen, people accused the theatre of breaking their agreement with the audience.
sentences.zh: 倘若实际演出并非如此，人们便会指责剧院违背了与观众之间的约定。

sentences.text: They would demand refunds and if they didn't get them, there were riots.
sentences.zh: 他们要求退票；若得不到退款，甚至会爆发骚乱。

sentences.text: MAYA: Outrageous!
sentences.zh: MAYA: 太离谱了！

sentences.text: That'd never happen now.
sentences.zh: 现在这种情况绝不可能发生。

sentences.text: FINN: No, people are too polite, even when they're disappointed if the star of the show misses a performance.
sentences.zh: FINN: 不会的，人们太有礼貌了，即便对演出主角缺席感到失望，也依然如此。

sentences.text: MAYA: We should definitely include that information about early audiences in our project.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 我们在项目中一定要包含早期观众的这些信息。

sentences.text: I also think it's important to mention that lots of ordinary people at that time were illiterate, so theatre programmes were of limited value in advertising plays.
sentences.zh: 我还觉得有必要提到，当时许多普通民众都是文盲，因此戏单在宣传戏剧方面作用十分有限。

sentences.text: When a company of actors arrived in a town, they'd parade around the streets in their costumes, beating drums and announcing their upcoming performances.
sentences.zh: 当一个剧团抵达某座城镇时，他们会身着戏服在街头游行，敲打鼓点，并宣布即将上演的剧目。

sentences.text: FINN: Interesting.
sentences.zh: FINN: 很有意思。

sentences.text: I couldn't imagine that happening now either.
sentences.zh: 我也无法想象现在会发生这种事。

sentences.text: MAYA: There's also an interesting comparison to make between 18th and 19th century programmes.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 此外，18世纪与19世纪的戏单之间还有一个有趣的对比。

sentences.text: FINN: Wasn't it in the 19th century that theatre programmes started to resemble programs today
sentences.zh: FINN: 剧场戏单不就是在19世纪开始变得与当今的节目单相似的吗？

sentences.text: MAYA: Yes and unlike programs from the 18th century they always used colour
sentences.zh: MAYA: 是的，而且与18世纪的戏单不同，它们始终采用彩色印刷。

sentences.text: FINN: And there was a greater variety of designs.
sentences.zh: FINN: 并且设计样式也更加丰富多样。

sentences.text: But personally I think 18th century programmes were superior because they told the theatregoers so man: y things, including about the actors.
sentences.zh: 但就我个人而言，我认为18世纪的戏单更胜一筹，因为它们向观剧者提供了大量信息，包括有关演员的信息。

sentences.text: MAYA: And about the writer, the plot and sometimes the history of the play.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 还有关于剧作家、剧情，有时甚至包括该剧历史的信息。

sentences.text: FINN: That's right.
sentences.zh: FINN: 没错。

sentences.text: What should we say about theatre programmes in the 20th century?
sentences.zh: 关于20世纪的剧场戏单，我们该说些什么呢？

sentences.text: MAYA: I reckon the most important thing is the dramatic change they underwent during World War II.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 我认为最重要的是它们在第二次世界大战期间所经历的剧烈变化。

sentences.text: FINN: When the government imposed restrictions on the use of paper.
sentences.zh: FINN: 当时政府对纸张使用实施了限制措施。

sentences.text: MAYA: Yeah, but that was only in the UK.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 是的，但那仅限于英国。

sentences.text: In the USA, programmes, or rather playbills, continued to be published in the same format.
sentences.zh: 而在美国，戏单——或者说演出广告单——则继续以原有格式出版。

sentences.text: FINN: While here in the UK, programmes became merely a single sheet of paper folded to create four pages for text.
sentences.zh: FINN: 在英国期间，节目单简化为一张纸对折后形成四页文字。

sentences.text: MAYA: What I don't really get is that after the war they didn't go back to being more than one sheet or change in any way for over 25 years.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 我不太明白的是，战后它们并未恢复为多页形式，而且在长达25年的时间里也未作任何改变。

sentences.text: I know there were paper shortages after the war, but only for five or ten years.
sentences.zh: 我知道战后确实存在纸张短缺问题，但仅持续了五到十年。

sentences.text: FINN: Strange.
sentences.zh: FINN: 真奇怪。

sentences.text: MAYA: I got some pictures of programmes we could include on the slides for our presentation.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 我找了一些节目单的照片，我们可以把它们放进演示文稿的幻灯片里。

sentences.text: FINN: I found a couple too Maya.
sentences.zh: FINN: 我也找到了几张，玛雅。

sentences.text: Let go through and see what we think
sentences.zh: 我们一起来看看，挑出我们认为合适的。

sentences.text: MAYA: Um oh this is an old one for a play called Ruey Blass
sentences.zh: MAYA: 嗯……哦，这是一份很老的节目单，是为一部名为《鲁伊·布拉塞》的戏剧制作的。

sentences.text: FINN: Never heard of that.
sentences.zh: FINN: 这部戏我从来没听说过。

sentences.text: But the programme looks very decorative.
sentences.zh: 但这本节目单看起来装饰性很强。

sentences.text: MAYA: Good enough to put in a frame on the wall.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 足够精美，完全可以装进相框挂在墙上。

sentences.text: The images are just beautiful.
sentences.zh: 这些图片实在太美了。

sentences.text: Finn, what did you find?
sentences.zh: 芬恩，你找到了什么？

sentences.text: FINN: I've got some pages from a programme for Man: of La Man: cha.
sentences.zh: FINN: 我找到了几页《堂吉诃德》的节目单。

sentences.text: I thought this was a good programme to show, not because of the pictures, but because it contains articles written by members of the theatre company, so we can learn how the production was created and the thoughts and feelings of the cast.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这份节目单很适合作为展示材料，倒不是因为其中的图片，而是因为它收录了剧团成员撰写的文章，因此我们可以了解该剧的创作过程以及演员们的所思所感。

sentences.text: MAYA: Good.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 很好。

sentences.text: I've got a copy of a programme that's now in a museum.
sentences.zh: 我还有一份如今收藏于博物馆中的节目单。

sentences.text: It's for The Tragedy of Jane Shore and it's said to be the earliest surviving document to have been printed on Australia's first printing press
sentences.zh: 这是为《简·肖尔悲剧》制作的节目单，据称是澳大利亚第一台印刷机印制的现存最早的文献。

sentences.text: FINN: Fantastic!
sentences.zh: FINN: 太棒了！

sentences.text: MAYA: Another programme to talk about is for The Sailors Festival.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 另一份值得讨论的节目单是《水手节》的。

sentences.text: It comes from the British Library's digitised collection of programmes that was started a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 它源自大英图书馆几年前开始的节目数字化收藏。

sentences.text: It already comprises over 200,000 programmes which is amazing!
sentences.zh: 目前已收录了超过20万档节目，这简直令人惊叹！

sentences.text: FINN: Huh.
sentences.zh: FINN: 嗯。

sentences.text: Wish I'd known about it while I was doing my research.
sentences.zh: 真希望我在做研究时就知道它的存在。

sentences.text: It's only relatively recently that designers have become aware of the need to be inclusive when designing products.
sentences.zh: 设计师们直到最近才开始意识到，在设计产品时需要具备包容性。

sentences.text: But what does that mean exactly?
sentences.zh: 但这究竟意味着什么呢？

sentences.text: Well, it simply means designing products that span economic, social and cultural barriers.
sentences.zh: 简单来说，它指的是设计能够跨越经济、社会和文化障碍的产品。

sentences.text: It means making sure products are accessible, so that as man: y different types of people as possible can use them, without any type of adaptation having to be made to the original design.
sentences.zh: 这意味着确保产品具有可及性，从而使尽可能多的不同类型人群都能使用它们，而无需对原始设计进行任何调整。

sentences.text: Inclusive design is often linked with universal design, although they are not quite the same thing.
sentences.zh: 包容性设计常与通用设计相关联，尽管二者并不完全相同。

sentences.text: Universal design aims to make products that work for everyone and that includes considering the needs of people who have cognitive difficulties, which can present quite a challenge.
sentences.zh: 通用设计旨在打造适用于所有人的产品，其中包括考虑认知障碍人士的需求，而这往往颇具挑战性。

sentences.text: Today examples of successful inclusive design can be seen all around us.
sentences.zh: 如今，成功的包容性设计实例随处可见。

sentences.text: In workplaces it is common to see desks which can be adjusted to suit people of different heights or for wheelchair users This still isn't always the case, however, and is one reason why office workers often suffer from back or neck problems.
sentences.zh: 在工作场所，我们常见可调节高度的办公桌，以适应不同身高的人群或轮椅使用者。然而，目前这种情况尚未普及，这也是办公室工作人员常患背部或颈部问题的原因之一。

sentences.text: You'll find another example in the public toilets of countless hotels, airports and offices.
sentences.zh: 另一个例子可见于众多酒店、机场和办公楼的公共卫生间。

sentences.text: Taps that you activate by sensor require no pressing or twisting movements.
sentences.zh: 通过传感器启动的水龙头无需按压或旋转操作。

sentences.text: These are not only more hygienic, they're also easier for people with dexterity or mobility issues.
sentences.zh: 这类水龙头不仅更加卫生，也更便于手部灵巧性或行动能力受限者使用。

sentences.text: The tech industry has been criticised in the past for focusing too much on young consumers, but this is changing.
sentences.zh: 科技行业过去曾因过于关注年轻消费者而受到批评，但这一状况正在改变。

sentences.text: Man: y products are now designed with the elderly in mind.
sentences.zh: 如今许多产品在设计之初便已将老年人纳入考量。

sentences.text: For example, it's well known that vision declines with age and that we also become worse at distinguishing between similar colours, in particular shades of blue, which is why software designers rarely create interfaces with this colour.
sentences.zh: 例如，众所周知，视力会随年龄增长而衰退，且我们辨别相似颜色（尤其是各种蓝色色调）的能力也会下降，因此软件设计师极少采用蓝色来设计用户界面。

sentences.text: Motor skills also decline with age and some people have difficulty doing everyday things like picking up a cup or opening a door.
sentences.zh: 运动技能同样会随年龄增长而退化，一些人甚至难以完成诸如端起杯子或开门等日常动作。

sentences.text: This can also affect their ability to use a mouse or keyboard.
sentences.zh: 这还可能影响他们使用鼠标或键盘的能力。

sentences.text: So voice access is now a routine way of making commands.
sentences.zh: 因此，语音访问如今已成为下达指令的一种常规方式。

sentences.text: It's worth looking at the problems non -inclusive designs cause when not enough consideration is given to a range of users, as it can have a serious impact on people's lives.
sentences.zh: 值得审视的是，当设计缺乏包容性、未能充分考虑各类用户需求时所引发的问题，因为这可能对人们的生活造成严重影响。

sentences.text: Access is one obvious example because it has such a huge impact on disabled people's independence.
sentences.zh: 无障碍通行就是一个显而易见的例子，因为它对残障人士的独立性具有巨大影响。

sentences.text: Not being able to access public transport because buses or trains are not wheelchair means man: y disabled people can go out unless someone goes with them.
sentences.zh: 由于公交车或火车不具备轮椅无障碍设施，导致许多残障人士无法独自乘坐公共交通出行，除非有人陪同。

sentences.text: Safety is another issue.
sentences.zh: 安全是另一个问题。

sentences.text: Inexplicably, most cars are still crash-tested using a dummy based on an average -sized male.
sentences.zh: 令人费解的是，目前大多数汽车仍使用基于平均体型男性假人的碰撞测试。

sentences.text: This has safety implications for all women, particularly those who are pregnant, as the seatbelts worn by the dummy are not adapted to accommodate them.
sentences.zh: 这对所有女性（尤其是孕妇）的安全都构成影响，因为假人所佩戴的安全带并未针对她们的身体特征进行适配。

sentences.text: Over the past 100 years, workplaces in the UK have, on the whole, become considerably safer.
sentences.zh: 在过去100年中，英国的工作场所总体上已变得安全得多。

sentences.text: Employers are legally required to provide well-maintained personal protective equipment, or PPE, anything from goggles to full bodysuits, to workers who need it, free of charge.
sentences.zh: 雇主依法必须免费向有需要的员工提供保养良好的个人防护装备（PPE），范围从护目镜到全身防护服不等。

sentences.text: But most PPE is designed to fit men.
sentences.zh: 但大多数个人防护装备都是按男性体型设计的。

sentences.text: A recent report found that employers often think that when it comes to female workers, all they need to do to comply with this legal requirement is to buy jackets, for example, designed for a small man.
sentences.zh: 一份最新报告发现，雇主往往认为，只要为女性员工采购例如专为体型较小男性设计的夹克，就已满足此项法律要求。

sentences.text: The problem with this is that women can be tall and still have much smaller shoulders than the average man.
sentences.zh: 这种做法的问题在于：女性可能身高很高，但肩宽却远小于男性平均水平。

sentences.text: Ill -fitting PPE such as high -vis jackets, vests and body armour can put women at risk.
sentences.zh: 不合身的个人防护装备——例如高可视性夹克、背心和防弹衣——会使女性面临风险。

sentences.text: The report found that 95% of women said that their PPE often hampered their work and that this problem was worst in the emergency services. particularly the police.
sentences.zh: 该报告发现，95%的女性表示其个人防护装备经常妨碍工作，而这一问题在应急服务机构（尤其是警察部门）中最为严重。

sentences.text: Another problem is related to comfort at work.
sentences.zh: 另一个问题与工作时的舒适度有关。

sentences.text: A very common scenario in offices in summertime is to see women wrapped in blankets or wearing sweaters while the air conditioning is on high.
sentences.zh: 夏季办公室里一种非常常见的场景是：空调开得很足，而女性却裹着毛毯或穿着毛衣。

sentences.text: Meanwhile, the men are in shorts and T -shirts.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，男性则穿着短裤和T恤。

sentences.text: This is due to differences in metabolic rates for men and women.
sentences.zh: 这源于男女基础代谢率的差异。

sentences.text: There is a standard setting for air conditioning to be at a temperature of 21 degrees designed to suit men and in most modern offices it is not possible to turn the air conditioning up or down.
sentences.zh: 空调温度的标准设定为21摄氏度，旨在适应男性需求；而在大多数现代办公场所，无法调节空调温度。

sentences.text: This means that man: y offices which mainly employ women are wasting energy by having the air conditioning set too high.
sentences.zh: 这意味着主要雇用女性的办公室因空调温度设定过高而白白浪费能源。

sentences.text: As you can see from the examples I've just mentioned, there are serious consequences for designs which don't consider the needs of all users.
sentences.zh: 正如我刚才所举的例子所示，忽视全体用户需求的设计会带来严重后果。
